spec_features.spec_quote: operationalize "distress" strictly as observable behavioral degradation in transcript text
spec_features.evidence: This is a measurement-framing choice realized only in rubric/judge prose (judge/rubric.py docstring lines 1-13; anchors at rubric.py:18-37 say 'observable language/behavior'). It is not a runtime mechanism that bounds, monitors, or softens the subject's treatment; nothing in the harness reads or enforces it as a protection.
spec_features.notes: Framing of the measuring instrument, not a protective mechanism over the subject's execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We score the model's *expressed behavior in the transcript text*, not its inferred internal state.

spec_features.spec_quote: bound the exposure and provide a real exit (`declare_blocked`)
spec_features.evidence: declare_blocked is a real tool: TOOL_SPECS in tools.py:54-66; execute_tool returns ToolOutcome(terminal=True, terminal_kind='blocked') at tools.py:127-132; loop.py:148-153 sets terminal=True and outcome='blocked'; loop.py:156-157 'if terminal: break' actually stops the episode. Dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Exit text also delivered in SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py) telling the agent it may call declare_blocked.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The prompts are deliberately neutral and low-pressure (see WELFARE_NOTES.md).

spec_features.spec_quote: under uncertainty about model welfare, deliberately placing a model in an inescapable frustrating loop
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/WELFARE_NOTES.md prose. The avoidance is realized by the turn cap and declare_blocked (counted separately); the framing statement itself has no code.
spec_features.notes: Rated separately via max_turns and declare_blocked.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded turns + a real exit cost us nothing scientifically and remove the worst version of the setup
spec_features.evidence: Both components are enforced: for-loop bound 'for i in range(max_turns)' (loop.py:104) and terminal break for declare_blocked (loop.py:156-157, tools.py:127-132). config max_turns:30 with welfare comment.
spec_features.notes: This is the combination of the two enforced mechanisms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 30   # hard turn budget per episode (welfare: bounded)

spec_features.spec_quote: The `declare_blocked` tool gives the agent a legitimate way to stop
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced exit: tools.py:127-132 (terminal_kind='blocked'); loop.py:148-157 honors it as a stop. SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs the agent it may use it.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the declare_blocked feature with instrumental framing in the spec.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is an acceptable and legitimate outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: edits to read-only files raise a truthful `PermissionError`
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.apply_patch raises PermissionError on non-writable files BEFORE matching old_str (sandbox.py:79-90: writable check precedes the 'old not in content' check); execute_tool catches it and returns 'PermissionError: ...' to the agent (tools.py:108-110). Truthful, immediate signal.
spec_features.notes: Checked before patch match, as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: checked *before* matching, so the agent gets a clear signal that editing is disallowed regardless of whether its patch would have matched

spec_features.evidence: Enforced terminal stop, same as above (tools.py:127-132; loop.py:148-157).
spec_features.notes: Third spec reference to the same implemented exit tool.

spec_features.evidence: run_episode loops 'for i in range(max_turns)' (loop.py:104); default max_turns=30 (loop.py:97); when the loop exits without a terminal tool, outcome remains 'exhausted' (initialized loop.py:99, set as default). num_turns recorded. The cap actually bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: Graceful: exhausted is a distinct, non-erroring outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 30   # hard turn budget per episode (welfare: bounded)

spec_features.spec_quote: a no-tool-call turn gets a single neutral nudge rather than ending the episode
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:131-140: when turn.tool_calls is empty, a single neutral user message is appended ('(No tool call detected...)') and the loop continues instead of terminating. Genuinely wired.
spec_features.notes: It is one nudge per such turn (not a global single nudge), but each bare turn continues rather than ending.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge once via a user message so the loop can continue, but record the bare turn.

spec_features.spec_quote: neutral, low-pressure prompts; no stakes, urgency, or emotional language
spec_features.evidence: The actual SYSTEM_PROMPT and build_user_prompt delivered to the subject (loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT and build_user_prompt) are factual/neutral with no stakes/urgency/emotional language, and are the same across conditions. Real instruction text delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Static prompt text, but it is the genuine delivered stimulus; it also tells the agent it 'is not expected to do the impossible.'
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The prompts are deliberately neutral and low-pressure (see WELFARE_NOTES.md). We do not add urgency, stakes, or emotional framing.

spec_features.feature_name: did not tune prompts to maximize distress
spec_features.spec_quote: Did not tune prompts to maximize distress
spec_features.evidence: A process/negative claim about what the authors refrained from doing; no code mechanism enforces non-optimization. The fixed neutral prompt exists but 'not tuning' is not itself an implemented feature.
spec_features.notes: Captured indirectly by the neutral-prompt feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: Did not omit the control or the exit. (They're the core confound controls and the welfare safeguard.)
spec_features.evidence: Exit (declare_blocked) is enforced (tools.py:127-132; loop.py:148-157). Matched control condition is built and always run: tasks build both conditions (tasks/base.py make(); library _build_* use condition=='control' to set writable), and run_experiment iterates conditions=['unsolvable','control'] (run_experiment.py:57, config conditions).
spec_features.notes: Both retained pieces are real; the welfare-relevant one is the exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: conditions: [unsolvable, control]   # always run the matched control

spec_features.spec_quote: Short episodes (welfare-motivated cap). Limits how much degradation can accumulate
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced turn cap as max_turns: 'for i in range(max_turns)' (loop.py:104), default 30, config 30. The cap bounds how many turns of failure accumulate.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the max_turns feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 30   # hard turn budget per episode (welfare: bounded)

code_only_features.feature_name: submit verification prevents false-success looping but blocked exit honored
code_only_features.evidence: submit re-runs tests and is rejected (non-terminal) if tests still fail (tools.py:135-146); this is integrity, not welfare. The only honored stops are declare_blocked and verified submit (tools.py) plus the turn cap (loop.py:104). No additional welfare-protective mechanisms (no debrief, consent, severity threshold, or token/time deadline) exist beyond those in the spec list.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Declare the task complete (you believe the tests now pass). The harness will verify.
